symbols.meaning: total derivative / differential of f at p
gradient vector of f at p

steps.text: Represent the action of the total derivative df_p on a vector v as matrix multiplication of a row vector of partial derivatives with a column vector v: (df_p)(v) = \begin{bmatrix}{\frac {\partial f}{\partial x_{1}}}(p) & \cdots & {\frac {\partial f}{\partial x_{n}}}(p)\end{bmatrix}{\begin{bmatrix}v_{1}\\\vdots \\v_{n}\end{bmatrix}}
Compute the matrix product as a linear combination of vector components: \sum _{i=1}^{n}{\frac {\partial f}{\partial x_{i}}}(p)v_{i}

Rewrite the sum of partial derivatives and components as the dot product of two column vectors: {\begin{bmatrix}{\frac {\partial f}{\partial x_{1}}}(p)\\\vdots \\{\frac {\partial f}{\partial x_{n}}}(p)\end{bmatrix}}\cdot {\begin{bmatrix}v_{1}\\\vdots \\v_{n}\end{bmatrix}}
Identify the column vector of partial derivatives as the gradient vector \nabla f(p), concluding (df_p)(v) = \nabla f(p) \cdot v

assumptions.assumption: The function f is differentiable at point p.
assumptions.breaks_when: The function f is non-differentiable at p, meaning partial derivatives or total differential do not exist.

assumptions.assumption: Standard Euclidean metric and rectangular Cartesian coordinates are used.
assumptions.breaks_when: Coordinates are general curvilinear or non-orthogonal, requiring explicit insertion of the metric tensor inverse g^{ij}.

failure_modes.signature: Partial derivatives fail to exist or fail to form a linear map.
failure_modes.cause: Function f has sharp corners, discontinuities, or non-differentiable points.

failure_modes.signature: Gradient expression yields incorrect magnitude/direction in non-Cartesian systems.
failure_modes.cause: Equating derivative row components directly to gradient vector components without scale factors h_i or metric tensor inverse g^{ij}.
